title: This Fish Is the Kobayashi of the Sea - Nautilus
gist: A deep-sea survey around Trinidad and Tobago aboard the Falkor found 20 potential new species and filmed a black swallower that had consumed prey up to 10 times its mass.

insights.claim: SpeSeas marine biologists aboard the Schmidt Ocean Institute's ship Falkor completed the most comprehensive deep-sea survey around Trinidad and Tobago, discovering 20 potential new species.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Shows how much deep-sea biodiversity remains uncatalogued.
insights.locator: Hosted aboard the Schmidt Ocean Institute's ship Falkor

insights.claim: An ROV at about 1,259 meters filmed a black swallower (Chiasmodon niger) that had eaten prey many times its body size.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: The black swallower grows only 4 to 8 inches long yet eats fish up to four times its length and 10 times its mass whole, dislocating its jaw and distending its stomach.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Extreme feeding adaptation of deep-sea predators.
